title: SCODEL: Shared Canonical Ontology Definitions for Food Entity Linking and Ontology-Grounded Recipe Knowledge Graphs
abstract: arXiv:2610.27637v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Identifying recipe entities and linking them to ontology concepts is fundamental for semantic recipe understanding. However, food mentions in recipes are often ambiguous, context-dependent, and lexically diverse, making ontology entity linking (EL) challenging. We propose SCODEL, a streamlined, model-agnostic approach based on a central idea: contextual food mentions and ontology concepts that refer to the same entity should learn the same canonical ontology-oriented definition. SCODEL uses these shared definitions as a semantic normalisation layer, providing complementary semantic information to existing EL models without requiring a new linking architecture. We further introduce ReciLinkD, the first benchmark for contextual food ontology entity linking in recipes. Experiments show that SCODEL consistently improves three modular EL models (ReFinED, GSM-EL, and BLINK): SCODEL x BLINK achieves the highest Hit@1 on seen concepts (88.33%),

translated_title: SCODEL：用于食物实体链接与基于本体的食谱知识图谱的共享规范本体定义
translated_abstract: 识别食谱实体并将其链接到本体概念是语义化食谱理解的基础。然而，食谱中的食物提及往往是模糊的、依赖上下文的且词汇形式多样的，这使得本体实体链接（EL）面临挑战。我们提出了SCODEL，这是一种简洁的、与模型无关的方法，其核心思想是：指向同一实体的上下文食物提及和本体概念应当学习相同的规范化面向本体的定义。SCODEL将这些共享定义用作语义规范化层，为现有的EL模型提供互补的语义信息，而无需引入新的链接架构。我们还进一步推出了ReciLinkD，这是首个针对食谱中上下文食物本体实体链接的基准数据集。实验表明，SCODEL能够持续提升三个模块化EL模型（ReFinED、GSM-EL和BLINK）的性能：SCODEL x BLINK在已见概念上达到了最高的Hit@1（88.33%）。
tldr: SCODEL通过让上下文食物提及与本体概念学习相同的规范化本体定义作为语义规范化层，无需新架构即可持续提升现有实体链接模型的性能，并发布了首个食谱上下文食物本体实体链接基准数据集ReciLinkD。
en_tdlr: SCODEL improves food ontology entity linking by learning shared canonical ontology definitions as a semantic normalization layer that boosts existing EL models without new architectures, and introduces ReciLinkD, the first benchmark for contextual food entity linking in recipes.
